page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores running at 3.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware platform supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptography instructions. The instance includes no bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and it does not feature hardware GPU acceleration. Persistent disk operations require network-attached Premium Storage volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the E48as_v6 demonstrates strong computational and memory performance. It places in the top 25% of tested systems for PassMark CPU (63005.09), stress-ng multi-core execution (73848.76), and multi-core Geekbench (17835.0). In-memory database throughput is high, achieving 67.71 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and leading results in PassMark database operations (22371.21). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 273.3 GB/sec, and cached small-block memory reads reach 3648.82 GB/sec. Uncached memory bandwidth measures 113.13 GB/sec for reads and 83.12 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the middle 50% percentile range.

The instance delivers high compute density paired with substantial RAM, offering qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive deployments by minimizing the need for distributed clustering. The lack of local NVMe storage represents a architectural tradeoff, making I/O performance dependent on remote storage configuration. Additionally, while AVX-512 BF16 accelerates small model CPU inference, larger models present clear throughput limits, with 70B parameter text generation measuring 2.58 tokens per second. The E48as_v6 is primarily suited for large in-memory caches such as Redis, enterprise relational database systems, Clang software compilation pipelines, and memory-heavy analytics workloads.

The instance includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, utilizing remote Premium Storage instead.
